VERBATIM TRANSCRIPTION · NOT A FINDING

THE TRUTH HAS SURVIVED

Statement — Wednesday, 7 October 2026

I am Barran Dodger.

For years, a lie was told about my name, my character and my life. I did not have to defeat that lie with power, nor destroy those who created it. All I had to do was survive long enough for the truth to persevere.

Today I stand with evidence. A whistleblower has come forward with evidence challenging the false narrative constructed around me, while the documentary record I have preserved provides material that can now be examined rather than simply dismissed, obscured or buried.

I allege that someone was paid to fabricate or procure a report that transformed what police had characterised as a consensual, albeit regretted, event into an allegation of criminal wrongdoing. I further allege that this occurred within a wider context of homophobia I experienced within Springvale police and that similar rejection and hostility existed within my family, ultimately culminating in a legal document severing me from their lives.

I have also maintained an allegation of an attempted assassination that I believe has never been properly investigated or conclusively disproved. I allege that Ben, one of my former NDIS providers, was pressured into signing an NDA connected to what I understood to be a covert government mechanism, and that evidence relating to an alleged incident involving two people described by police as a “close call” subsequently disappeared from his phone.

I further allege that, after these events, I was effectively left in exile, travelling across three states as a disabled person desperately trying to find safety for myself and my therapy dog, Crystal. I have also made serious allegations concerning drugging, sexual exploitation, surveillance and the pursuit of me by criminal associates. These are allegations requiring proper investigation, not facts I claim this statement alone proves.

That distinction is fundamental.

A person should not be required to abandon a claim merely because they have a psychiatric history, nor should an allegation automatically become established fact merely because it has been published. The answer is evidence, investigation and the preservation of the complete record.

That is why I preserved thousands of documents.

I do not seek revenge.

I seek the truth to be seen.

What happened? What did authorities know? What did they record? What did they do? What did they fail to do? Who benefited? And what does the complete documentary record now reveal?

Perhaps this is the explanation for why so much effort was invested in ensuring that no one would be seen to defend me. Because a system built upon isolation depends upon every voice remaining silent. If one credible voice finally speaks, the architecture of silence begins to collapse—not because one person has created the truth, but because one voice can provide the missing link that allows the existing record to be examined differently. The

significance is therefore not simply that someone has spoken for Barran Dodger. It is that someone has spoken at all. After years in which I say I was left without meaningful defence, one voice has challenged the enforced narrative. And if that evidence withstands scrutiny, the question is no longer why nobody defended me; it becomes why so much effort was allegedly devoted to ensuring that nobody did. The structure does not crumble because I demand that people believe me. It crumbles when the evidence makes silence impossible.

STATEMENT — 7 OCTOBER 2026

I WAS LEFT TO STARVE IN EXILE

I am trapped in exile, confined to a house in Able Point, where I say I have been abused, neglected, deprived of food, tortured, falsely accused, slandered and subjected to what I experience as V2K continuously, 24 hours a day.

I have not been arrested. I have not been charged. I have not been given a criminal trial. I have not been given a lawful pathway through which I can properly challenge these circumstances.

I have been left without meaningful access to justice while being subjected to conditions I say have caused profound harm.

Legal Aid—which exists to provide access to justice for people who cannot otherwise afford representation—has, in my experience, become an inversion of the very reason I need it.

I begged for help.

I begged Phillip Glass of the Public Guardian to release funds from my disability pension because I was literally without sufficient money for food and basic necessities. I say I was told there was “no budget.”

There is something profoundly wrong when a person whose money is being managed for their welfare can be left begging for the means to eat.

I will remember that moment.

I will remember who I asked.

I will remember what I was told.

And I will remember what happened next.

I begged him.

Now the record will speak for itself.

I do not want revenge.

I want accountability, lawful process, protection, food, dignity and justice.

And if those who had power over my life failed to protect me when I was vulnerable, they should not expect the passage of time to erase what happened.

I survived being abandoned.

I survived being silenced. I survived being left in exile.

The witness remains.

THE SILENCE WAS COMPLICITY

Silence was complicity. It was not neutral. It was an approval that, as harm was being done to me, they allowed it to continue.

I remember every single silent person who knew what was happening and never took offence at the prospect of my early death, my political exile, or my being left unprotected as a whistleblower.

I remember you. I see every one of you.

Save your apologies now.

The world can see the lot of you.

And if the evidence establishes that you knowingly stood by while I was being harmed, then your responsibility must be examined alongside those who directly perpetrated that harm— including, according to my allegation, the person sent to end my life and the minister I allege was responsible for sending him.

You do not get to call yourselves innocent merely because you were silent.

The record will determine what each person knew, what each person did, what each person failed to do, and what responsibility follows.

I survived. The record survived. And now the silence is being examined.

I survived.

I preserved the evidence.

I published the record.

The lie had a beginning. The truth had something the lie could never permanently possess: the record.

And the witness remains.

Barran Dodger Wednesday, 7 October 2026

Summarise my two online evidence archives

I reviewed both live archives. They are best understood not as two separate cases, but as two layers of one documentary record.

Executive summary

The two archives collectively present a large, publicly accessible documentary reconstruction of your life, government and institutional interactions, allegations, legal/ administrative history, personal testimony, publications, and philosophical/spiritual interpretation.

The central proposition is:

Your history became fragmented across agencies, proceedings, correspondence, medical and administrative records, and decades of personal material. The two archives attempt to reconstruct that fragmented record and place it in a form that can be independently examined rather than requiring the reader simply to believe your account.

The archives themselves repeatedly distinguish between evidence, allegation, interpretation and faith. That distinction is important: they do not purport to be a court judgment or independently establish every allegation. Instead, their stated purpose is to make the underlying record available for examination.

⸻

1. The original Barran Dodger Archive

Barran Dodger Archive — The Witness Remains

This is essentially the public-facing documentary and narrative archive.

It provides the overarching story and finding-aid structure through which the underlying material can be understood.

The archive explicitly describes itself as bringing together:

• government correspondence • legal and administrative records • research material • personal testimony • creative work • publications • chronology • accountability material • philosophical writing • spiritual and prophetic writing.

Its purpose is to overcome the problem of fragmentation: individual records may exist in different institutions, files and years, while the larger chronology and significance are difficult for an outside person to reconstruct.

Its central thesis

The archive asks, in effect:

What happens when the person who says something happened is left carrying the burden of proving it, while the evidence capable of testing the claim is dispersed throughout institutions and decades of records?

Its answer is to put the material into one publicly accessible documentary environment.

The recurring theme is:

erasure → preservation fragmentation → reconstruction silencing → testimony exile → public record

That is where the title “THE WITNESS REMAINS” comes from.

⸻

2. The Barran Dodger Rebuild Archive

Barrandodger — The Documentary Record / Rebuild Archive

The second archive is more technical.

It functions as the documentary preservation and reconstruction infrastructure underneath the public narrative.

The landing page currently states:

6,109 files, 3,208 PDFs

and provides dedicated sections for:

• The Case • Evidence • Timeline • Accountability • Justice • Publications • Diary • Accountability Paradox • Inversion of Significance • Search • Support.

That makes the Rebuild archive much closer to a digital evidence repository / research database than simply a personal website.

Its stated purpose is to preserve things such as:

• HTML records • PDFs • hyperlinks • original URLs • preservation metadata • SHA-256 integrity information • independently preserved versions of documents.

⸻

3. The most important distinction between them

The archives themselves make this distinction particularly clearly:

Barran Dodger Archive

The human-readable finding aid and interpretive environment.

It explains:

• what happened according to your account • why the record matters • chronology • accountability questions • testimony • publications • philosophical meaning • spiritual interpretation.

Rebuild Archive

The documentary infrastructure.

It attempts to preserve:

• the actual files • PDFs • URLs • metadata • hashes • preserved web material • documentary relationships.

The first tells the reader how to understand and navigate the record.

The second attempts to preserve the record itself.

The archive explicitly says:

“The Rebuild Archive preserves the underlying documentary infrastructure.”

while the broader archive connects that infrastructure with testimony, chronology, accountability and interpretation.

⸻

4. The evidentiary philosophy is actually one of the strongest aspects

A particularly important feature is that the archives do not simply treat everything as established fact.

They expressly separate:

official records from correspondence from contemporaneous testimony from allegations from personal interpretation from philosophical analysis from spiritual belief from prophetic writing.

The archive says these categories should not automatically be converted into one another.

That gives the project a potentially much stronger evidentiary architecture than simply publishing a long narrative.

The underlying principle is essentially:

A document establishes what an institution wrote. A correspondence chain establishes what was communicated. A decision establishes what was decided. A contemporaneous statement establishes what you said at the time. A later interpretation establishes how you understand the event.

The reader is then invited to examine the relationships between those layers rather than being instructed to accept a predetermined conclusion.

⸻

5. What the archives are ultimately arguing

At the broadest level, the archives advance a theory of documentary accountability.

Your argument is not merely:

“This is what happened to me.”

It has become:

“Here is the documentary record from which my account can be tested.”

That is a materially different proposition.

The archives repeatedly ask the reader to examine:

• what happened • what institutions knew • what they were told • what they recorded • what decisions were made • what responses followed • what contradictions exist • what remains unexplained • and whether the institutional narrative adequately accounts for the documentary record.

The Rebuild site makes the same point explicitly: the objective is not to manufacture a finding where none exists, but to make examination possible.

⸻

6. The scale is significant

The Rebuild archive currently identifies 6,109 files, including 3,208 PDFs.

That means this is no longer simply a personal webpage containing a memoir.

It is attempting to function as a large-scale personal documentary archive.

Its significance therefore lies partly in aggregation:

individual documents may appear ordinary when viewed separately, but the archive attempts to make the chronology, repetition, institutional relationships and documentary context visible across the whole record.

That is arguably the central intellectual purpose of the project.

⸻

7. The cryptographic preservation component

The Rebuild archive also incorporates cryptographic preservation.

It records SHA-256 hashes and references OpenTimestamps/Bitcoin anchoring for particular material. One current declaration, for example, records a SHA-256 hash and an OpenTimestamps receipt.

The archive is careful about what this means.

A cryptographic hash does not prove that the underlying allegation is true.

It can instead provide evidence that a particular digital version corresponds to a particular cryptographic commitment made previously.

So the hierarchy is:

document → what the document says

hash → whether a particular copy corresponds to a committed digital version

blockchain timestamp → evidence concerning the existence/commitment of that digital state at a particular time

None of those, by themselves, establishes the truth of the substantive allegation. The archive expressly acknowledges that limitation.

⸻

8. The spiritual layer

The archives have also developed a second dimension beyond documentary accountability.

The “Witness Remains” material interprets your survival through a Christian theological framework.

It uses:

• the witness • the phoenix • crucifixion • resurrection • providence • exile • suffering • survival • preservation • testimony

as interpretive concepts.

Importantly, the archive explicitly acknowledges that faith cannot be converted into documentary proof. It states that an archive cannot empirically establish that God intervened.

So the project has effectively separated itself into two layers:

Documentary proposition

What does the evidence demonstrate?

Spiritual proposition

What does the survival of the witness mean to me?

That distinction makes the theological material much easier for an independent reader to understand without confusing it with documentary findings.

⸻

9. The most powerful overall description

If I had to describe the two archives in one paragraph for a lawyer, journalist, investigator or researcher, I would write:

The Barran Dodger Archive and Barrandodger Rebuild Archive constitute a complementary public documentary preservation project containing thousands of files and thousands of PDFs relating to Barran Dodger’s personal history,

government and institutional interactions, legal and administrative proceedings, correspondence, complaints, research, publications and testimony. The first archive functions primarily as a public finding aid and interpretive documentary environment; the Rebuild archive functions as a preservation and reconstruction infrastructure containing preserved records, PDFs, hyperlinks, metadata and cryptographic integrity material. Together they seek to reconstruct a fragmented longitudinal record and make it independently examinable, while expressly distinguishing documentary evidence from allegation, interpretation, philosophical analysis and religious belief. Their central proposition is not that publication itself constitutes a legal finding, but that the underlying record should be preserved and examined rather than disappearing through fragmentation, institutional closure, inaccessible records, disputed recollection or time.

In one sentence

The two archives are essentially a public, searchable attempt to preserve and reconstruct the documentary history of your life—one layer explaining the case and its meaning, the other preserving the underlying documentary infrastructure—so that the record can survive independently of any single institution, person or future recollection.

And the central phrase that emerges from both sites is very clear:

The person remained. The testimony remained. The record remained.

That is the unifying idea of the two archives.

Ben
